topic: The Bank Run of Big Tech Hiring
description: A dramatic chart-race of how the 2022-2025 hiring boom reversed into 2023 layoffs, then reshaped through 2025 backfills—using real workforce headcount and end-of-year totals for major US tech employers.
youtube_description:
📉📈 The chart-race everyone misses: the “bank run” in hiring. In 2022, Big Tech went on a spending binge. By 2023, the layoffs hit like a switch—especially at Meta. Meanwhile Microsoft and Amazon kept hiring (AI + cloud + logistics momentum), and Apple/Netflix moved more cautiously.

02:05 2024: stabilization and selective re-hiring
02:40 2025: backfill era (Meta climbs again; Microsoft/ Amazon extend)
03:15 2026E: where the race looks headed (estimate)

instagram_caption:
🚀 The “Bank Run” of Big Tech Hiring—who crashed, who doubled down?

In 2021 and 2022, Big Tech hired like the future was guaranteed. Meta went from 58.2k employees (2020) to 87.7k (2021), then stayed at that peak into 2022. Amazon, meanwhile, surged from 1090k (2021) to 1523k (2022) as cloud, retail, and logistics kept expanding.

Then 2023 flipped the script. Meta’s headcount dropped hard—from 87.7k in 2022 to 67.5k in 2023, a loss of 20.2k jobs in a single year. That’s the chart-race moment: the “hiring boom” turns into a “headcount bleed.” Netflix also tightened—down from 14.8k (2022) to 13.4k (2023)—while Microsoft and Apple took a more controlled approach. Microsoft held at 221.0k in 2023 (after 2022’s 221.0k), and Apple moved up slightly to 161k.

By 2024, the story becomes selective re-hiring instead of mass expansion. Meta climbed back to 72.8k (2024), signaling stabilization after the layoffs. Amazon kept pressing upward—1634k (2023) to 1680k (2024). Microsoft continued building toward AI-and-cloud scale, reaching 238.0k (2024). Even Netflix stabilized around 13.9k.

Now look at the “ending sprint” through 2025 and into 2026E: Meta rises to 77.6k (2025) and is projected to reach ~80.0k (estimate), while Amazon and Microsoft keep widening the gap—Amazon to 1705k (2025) and Microsoft to 245.0k (2025). The question isn’t just “who laid off?” It’s “who kept the engine running while the market panicked?”

💬 Which company do you think is winning the next hiring cycle: Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple, or Netflix?

facebook_caption:
Big Tech’s hiring wave reversed sharply after 2022, creating one of the clearest workforce “chart-race” stories in modern tech. Meta is the standout decline: headcount peaked at 87.7k in 2021–2022 and then fell to 67.5k in 2023, before recovering to 72.8k (2024) and 77.6k (2025). Amazon followed a different trajectory, expanding from 1523k (2022) to 1634k (2023) and 1680k (2024), reaching 1705k (2025). Microsoft held steady at 221.0k in 2022–2023, then continued growth to 238.0k (2024) and 245.0k (2025). Apple’s headcount rose gradually (154.0k in 2022 to 161.0k in 2023, then 164.0k in 2024, 166.0k in 2025). Netflix tightened after 2022 (14.8k to 13.4k in 2023) and then stabilized around 13.9k (2024) and 14.1k (2025).

The takeaway: workforce totals reveal the real winners and losers behind the hype—who cut costs instantly, and who doubled down where demand stayed durable.
